en: The Philippine archipelago consists of exactly 7,641 islands, divided into three main island groups: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Taal Volcano in Batangas holds the record as one of the smallest active volcanoes in the world, standing just 311 meters tall.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a massive surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
Davao City is the largest city in the Philippines by land area, encompassing a huge 2,443 square kilometers of territory.
The Philippines is home to more than 200 mammal species, with over 100 of them being endemic and found nowhere else globally.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones or typhoons every year due to its location in the Pacific Typhoon Belt.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer navigable underground river flowing directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 97,030 hectares and protects over 600 fish species and 360 coral species in the Sulu Sea.
The San Juanico Bridge connects the islands of Samar and Leyte, stretching 2.16 kilometers across the narrow San Juanico Strait.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of at least 1,268 symmetrical mounds that rise 30 to 50 meters above the surrounding plains.
